self_support_reserve.note: Connecticut's 'darker shaded area' of the Schedule of Basic Child Support Obligations: if the noncustodial parent's own net weekly income (rounded to the nearest $10) falls at or below this per-child-count threshold, that parent is a 'low-income obligor' and the schedule is looked up using their income ALONE (not combined income) -- the dollar amount shown is their full obligation directly, with no proration and no childcare/health insurance add-ons. Thresholds confirmed by visually reading the shaded cells in the official schedule (Regs. Conn. State Agencies 46b-215a-2c(e)): $280/week for one child, rising to $480/week for six or more children.

deviation_note: Connecticut income figures in this calculator are WEEKLY net income, not monthly. As of 2026-08-01, Connecticut's guidelines schedule was overhauled: the income cap was raised from $4,000/week to $6,000/week combined net income, and a new three-parent worksheet was introduced. THIS CALCULATOR STILL USES THE OLD $4,000/WEEK SCHEDULE AND HAS NOT BEEN UPDATED for the post-2026-08-01 guidelines -- above $4,000/week combined net income, the amount shown at the $4,000 row is treated as the MINIMUM presumptive support obligation (courts may award more, decided case-by-case), but this no longer matches the current official schedule up to $6,000/week. Treat any result above $4,000/week combined net income as unreliable until this calculator is updated. This calculator models the standard (sole-custody) case only. It does not model Shared Physical Custody (Regs. Conn. State Agencies 46b-215a-1(23): when each parent has at least roughly equal time, the presumptive order equals the HIGHER-net-income parent's own calculated share, paid to the other parent, unadjusted for the specific time split), Split Custody (each parent primary for different children, calculated as an offset between two worksheets), or the new three-parent worksheet introduced 2026-08-01.
